newsitem.title: PARAGUAY: Paraguay raw cotton crop seen down at 300,000 T.
newsitem.headline: Paraguay raw cotton crop seen down at 300,000 T.

text.p: Paraguay's 1996/97 cotton harvest is expected to be around 300,000 tonnes of raw fiber, down from 332,000 in the 1995/96 season, a spokesman for the cotton chamber Cadelpa said Friday.
In a separate announcement, the government said late Thursday that for the first time in 15 years it will not help producers with soft credits or subsidies.
"There will be no incentives," Agriculture and Livestock Minister Juan Borgognon told a news conference.
Output of 300,000 tonnes would yield some 100,000 tonnes for export, the Cadelpa spokesman told Reuters.
Earlier estimates had put the 1996/97 harvest at 335,000 tonnes, but the spokesman said the area set aside for sowing and the amount of seed were heralding a much lower yield.
Sowing for the 1996/97 harvest starts later in September in the north, in October in the south and in November in the west.
Paraguay's best harvest was in 1990/91, with 753,000 tonnes of raw fiber.
